message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to accept, reject, or counter-trade with p2.

p2 offers $300 for VENTNOR_AVENUE. I have $292 cash and several properties. p1 has a pink monopoly and can build there. p2 just bought Marvin Gardens. p3 only owns the electric company.

Accepting the trade would give me $40 profit. But p2 would then own Ventnor and Marvin Gardens, leaving only Atlantic unowned to complete a yellow monopoly. That would strengthen p2 significantly.

I have no color set. p1 can build two houses on each pink property for $600, making rent dangerous. I am weighing whether to protect my yellow holdings or accept the trade.

I had misidentified p1's holdings. p1 does not have a pink monopoly. They own St. Charles and States but lack Virginia. They also lack Oriental for the light blues and only hold St. James for the oranges. I am now reassessing the actual threats.

Virginia Avenue is unowned. p1 does not have a pink monopoly. No player has a completed color set yet.

Boardwalk is the most urgent purchase. I need $400 but only have $292 cash. Accepting the trade would raise my balance to $592, giving me enough to buy Boardwalk and still hold $192. Ventnor is worth $40 over its list price.

I should reject the trade. Ventnor is worth more than its $40 premium because it blocks p2's yellow path and gives me leverage. Boardwalk is unowned, so p2 cannot provide it.

I considered trading Ventnor for Marvin Gardens, but that would give p2 both yellows and leave me with only one. That would be worse than the current offer. I will reject the trade.

I am reconsidering a high counter-offer of $800 or more for Ventnor to raise cash for Boardwalk. I will publicly reject the trade but leave the door open for a better deal later. A dark blue monopoly is the strongest color set in the game.

Mortgaging Reading Railroad and Ventnor would raise enough cash to buy Boardwalk without selling Ventnor. I can wait to land on it instead.

I rejected the idea of trading Reading Railroad for Marvin Gardens. p2 just bought Marvin and would not trade it away for a railroad. A counter would also reveal my strategy and weaken future negotiations. I will stick with a clean rejection.
